1738: When the French artists are not drawing whiskered grenadiers or ruffianly dragoons, or their eternal Emperor with his grey great coat and his hands behind him, they do not seem capable of producing anything beyond ballet dancers and Turkish odalisques, and brazen creatures in black velvet trousers and shirt sleeves, called, I believe, debardeurs.
